title: Trump Says Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Had 'No Idea' Extramarital Partner Was Chinese Agent
snippet: President Trump defended Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Monday, telling reporters the tech executive denied knowing his former mistress was a Chinese intelligence operative during a recent phone call.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump revealed Monday that he spoke directly with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang regarding allegations that the high-profile tech executive engaged in an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. Trump stated that Huang vehemently denied knowing the woman was a spy, an account the President said he finds credible.

Addressing reporters in the White House briefing room, Trump said he reached out to check on Huang following intense public and national security scrutiny.

"I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling all right," Trump told reporters. "I asked him about that, and he said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy. I asked him that question... and I really believe him."

Probes Underway into Foreign Intelligence Operations

Trump noted that federal authorities are currently probing the situation, confirming that the FBI is reviewing the intelligence concerns. Nvidia has also launched an internal investigation to evaluate whether Huang was intentionally targeted by a foreign intelligence service.

The revelation comes after Huang accompanied Trump on a state visit to Beijing last spring. Trump indicated he was unaware of any potential espionage risks during the trip and only learned of the intelligence concerns "not too long ago."

When questioned about whether intelligence agencies had previously briefed him regarding Huang's relationship, Trump acknowledged it might have come up in prior meetings. "They could have been mentioned. Certainly, it didn’t make much of an impact on me," Trump said.

Despite the federal and corporate investigations now underway, Trump expressed optimism regarding Huang's future, stating, "I think that he’ll be in good shape."
